_readme: Kid-friendly copy for LA Top Jobs. Edit words here, then run `python top_jobs/build_data.py` to merge in the latest LA Works forecasts and BLS wages. Numbers are NOT typed here; the build script fills them in from the official files. Each focus area's `group` names its group in occupations.csv; `soc` may list several codes (comma-separated), which are combined.

sectors.name: Skilled Trades
sectors.tagline: Build it, fix it, power it. Louisiana needs people who can work with their hands.

jobs.name: Carpenter
jobs.what: build and repair homes, businesses, and other buildings using wood and other materials. They make structures safe and sturdy.
jobs.path: Finish high school, then join a paid apprenticeship. You earn money while you learn.

jobs.name: Welder
jobs.what: use heat and special tools to join metal pieces together. They help build and repair machines, pipes, ships, and buildings.
jobs.path: Take a welding program at a community or technical college. Many take less than a year.

jobs.name: Electrician
jobs.what: install and repair the wiring and equipment that bring electricity to homes, schools, and businesses, so the lights stay on safely.
jobs.path: Finish high school, then join a paid apprenticeship (about 4 years). You earn money while you learn.

jobs.name: Industrial Mechanic
jobs.what: keep the big machines in factories and plants running. They find out what is broken and fix it fast.
jobs.path: Take an industrial maintenance program at a technical college, then keep learning on the job.

jobs.name: Plumber
jobs.what: install and fix the pipes that carry water and gas in homes, businesses, and factories.
jobs.path: Finish high school, then join a paid apprenticeship. You earn money while you learn.

sectors.name: Healthcare
sectors.tagline: Help people feel better. Hospitals and clinics across Louisiana are hiring.

jobs.name: Registered Nurse
jobs.what: care for patients in hospitals, clinics, and schools. They give medicine, check on patients, and work with doctors.
jobs.path: Earn a nursing degree (2 or 4 years) and pass the state nursing exam.

training.label: LSU Health New Orleans School of Nursing

jobs.name: Nurse Practitioner
jobs.what: are nurses with extra training. They can examine patients, figure out what is wrong, and prescribe medicine.
jobs.path: Become a registered nurse first, then earn a graduate degree in nursing.

training.label: LSU Health New Orleans School of Nursing

jobs.name: Nursing Assistant
jobs.what: help patients with everyday needs like eating, bathing, and moving around. They are often the first step into a nursing career.
jobs.path: Finish a short, state-approved training program (a few weeks) and pass a skills test.

jobs.name: Medical Assistant
jobs.what: keep doctors' offices running. They check patients in, take vital signs, and help doctors during exams.
jobs.path: Earn a certificate from a community or technical college. It usually takes about a year.

sectors.name: Tech & Engineering
sectors.tagline: Code it, design it, engineer it. Louisiana needs problem-solvers.

jobs.name: Software Developer
jobs.what: write the code behind apps, websites, and games. They plan how a program should work, then build and test it.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year degree in computer science or a related field.

jobs.name: Computer Support Specialist
jobs.what: help people when their computers, phones, or networks stop working. They find the problem and fix it.
jobs.path: Earn a certificate or 2-year degree in information technology. Industry certifications help you get hired.

jobs.name: Civil Engineer
jobs.what: design roads, bridges, levees, and water systems, and make sure they are built safely.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year engineering degree. Many go on to earn a state engineering license.

jobs.name: Computer Systems Analyst
jobs.what: study how a business uses computers and find ways to make its systems work better.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year degree in computer science or information systems.

jobs.name: Environmental Scientist
jobs.what: protect people and nature. They test air, water, and soil for pollution and find ways to clean it up.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year degree in environmental science, biology, or chemistry.

sectors.name: Business
sectors.tagline: Every company needs people who can manage money, people, and plans.

jobs.name: Accountant
jobs.what: keep track of money for businesses and families. They check records, prepare taxes, and help leaders make smart choices.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year degree in accounting. Many become Certified Public Accountants (CPAs).

jobs.name: HR & Training Specialist
jobs.what: hire new workers, help employees with pay and benefits, and teach training classes.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year degree in business, human resources, or a related field.

jobs.name: Marketing Specialist
jobs.what: help companies tell people about their products and share news with the public.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year degree in marketing, communications, or business.

jobs.name: Project Manager
jobs.what: keep big projects on schedule and on budget, from building a new plant to launching new software.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year degree, then build experience leading projects. Certifications can help.

jobs.name: Management Analyst
jobs.what: study how a business works and suggest ways to save money and work smarter.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year degree in business or a related field.

sectors.name: Transportation
sectors.tagline: Louisiana's highways, rivers, and ports need people to keep goods moving.

jobs.name: Truck Driver
jobs.what: deliver goods across town or across the country. Long-haul drivers carry big loads in tractor-trailers.
jobs.path: Finish high school, then earn a commercial driver's license (CDL) in a training program that takes a few weeks.

jobs.name: Deckhand
jobs.what: work on boats, barges, and ships. They help steer, keep watch, tie up the boat, and keep the engines running.
jobs.path: Start after high school with on-the-job training and a U.S. Coast Guard mariner credential.

jobs.name: Boat Captain
jobs.what: steer and command boats and ships, like tugboats pushing barges up the Mississippi River.
jobs.path: Work your way up from deckhand, take maritime training, and earn a U.S. Coast Guard license.

jobs.name: Forklift Operator
jobs.what: drive forklifts and other machines that move heavy materials in warehouses, plants, and ports.
jobs.path: Start after high school. Most training happens on the job, often with a short safety certification.

jobs.name: Cargo Loader
jobs.what: load and unload cargo from trucks, rail cars, and ships, and run pumps that move liquids like oil and chemicals.
jobs.path: Start after high school and learn on the job.

sectors.name: Teaching & Public Service
sectors.tagline: Teach, protect, and serve your community.

jobs.name: Teacher
jobs.what: help kids learn reading, math, science, and more, from kindergarten through high school.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year degree and a Louisiana teaching certificate.

jobs.name: Police Officer
jobs.what: protect people and keep communities safe. They answer calls, patrol neighborhoods, and help in emergencies.
jobs.path: Finish high school, then complete police academy training.

jobs.name: Special Education Teacher
jobs.what: teach students who learn in different ways, and change lessons so every student can succeed.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year degree and a special education teaching certificate.

jobs.name: School Counselor
jobs.what: help students with schoolwork, plans after graduation, and personal problems.
jobs.path: Earn a 4-year degree, then a master's degree in counseling.

jobs.name: Firefighter
jobs.what: put out fires, rescue people, and give emergency medical care.
jobs.path: Finish high school, complete fire academy training, and earn an EMT certification.
